title: Starting up a project: purpose, objectives and context
blurb: Explain why starting up a project exists, what it must achieve and how the project mandate triggers it before initiation.
question: Which process answers the question 'do we have a viable and worthwhile project?', and what triggers it?

teach.body: Formally: the purpose of starting up a project is to make sure the prerequisites for initiating a project are in place, by answering 'do we have a viable and worthwhile project?'. In plain English: before anyone spends time and money on initiation, a small amount of work checks the idea is sound, gets the right people in place and plans the initiation stage.

teach.h: Where starting up a project sits

steps.sub: From the business layer that commissions the project

Request project

teach.caption: The decision to start the project must be explicit, so starting up a project happens before that decision is made.

teach.body: Starting up a project is a lighter process than initiating a project. It does only the minimum needed to decide whether initiation is worthwhile. It is as much about stopping poorly conceived ideas from being initiated as it is about approving good ones. The project brief it produces gives everyone a commonly understood, well-defined starting point.

teach.h: What the board does with the result

root.label: Request to initiate
root.sub: Project brief and initiation stage plan

rows.label: Business layer: provides the mandate and is accountable for appointments
Executive: responsible for appointing the project manager and team
Project manager: prepares the brief and the initiation stage plan

teach.note: Starting up a project is the one process used by both the directing and managing levels. If the project is part of a programme, the programme may supply much of the brief.

teach.body: Ashdown Community Health Trust issues a mandate for a text reminder service to cut missed appointments. Executive Daniel Mensah appoints project manager Sunita Rao. Sunita keeps starting up short: an outline business case, a brief and an initiation stage plan. While testing assumptions she finds the planned supplier framework has expired, so the timescale is unsound. She records it in the brief before requesting initiation, so the board is not asked to fund initiation on a false premise.

teach.text: Classic traps: starting up a project is NOT the first stage (initiation is), and it does NOT produce the project plan or the full business case; those come in initiating a project. Its purpose is the 'viable and worthwhile?' question; 'solid foundations before significant spend' is the purpose of initiating a project.

items: Purpose: prerequisites for initiation in place; 'do we have a viable and worthwhile project?'.
Trigger: the project mandate from the business layer; it is pre-project.
Light: the minimum needed to decide; it also stops poorly conceived ideas.
Objectives: outline business case, authorities, brief, project approach, appointments, initiation stage plan, no unsound assumptions.
Ends with the request to initiate, which starts directing a project.

summary: You can now state the purpose and objectives of starting up a project and explain its context: triggered by the project mandate, pre-project, deliberately light and ending with a request to initiate. You can also tell it apart from initiating a project.

A.q: What is the purpose of the starting up a project process?
options: To establish solid foundations before committing significant spend
To ensure the prerequisites for initiating the project are in place
To enable the board to be accountable through key decisions
To assign work, monitor it and keep the stage within tolerance
A.why: Starting up a project ensures the prerequisites for initiating are in place by asking whether the project is viable and worthwhile (manual 13.1).

whyNot.0: Establishing solid foundations before significant spend is the purpose of initiating a project (15.1).
whyNot.2: Enabling the board to be accountable through key decisions is the purpose of directing a project (14.1).
whyNot.3: Assigning and monitoring work within stage tolerances is the purpose of controlling a stage.

A.q: What triggers the starting up a project process?
options: The initiation notice
The project brief
The business case
The project mandate
A.why: The project mandate, provided by the responsible authority in the business layer, triggers starting up a project (13.3).

whyNot.0: The initiation notice is issued by the board in authorize initiation and triggers initiating a project.
whyNot.1: The project brief is an output of starting up a project, not its trigger.
whyNot.2: Starting up produces an outline business case; a business case does not trigger the process.

A.q: Which question does starting up a project answer?
options: Do we have a viable and worthwhile project?
Is the stage still within its tolerances?
Are the products ready to hand over?
How will baselines be controlled?
A.why: Starting up a project asks 'do we have a viable and worthwhile project?' before the explicit decision to initiate (13.1).

whyNot.1: Checking the stage against its tolerances belongs to controlling a stage.
whyNot.2: Confirming products are ready for handover belongs to closing a project.
whyNot.3: How baselines are established and controlled is a common understanding reached in initiating a project.

B.q:
Which two statements describe objectives of starting up a project?
1. Ensure the business layer has a connection to the project.
2. Ensure there is business justification for initiating, in an outline business case.
3. Ensure the project plan for the whole project is approved.
4. Ensure alternative approaches are evaluated and the project approach agreed.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Justification for initiating (2) and an agreed project approach after evaluating alternatives (4) are objectives of starting up a project (13.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is an objective of directing a project, not starting up a project.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 is a directing a project objective, and statement 3 is wrong: the project plan is created in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is false: the project plan is prepared in initiating a project and approved when the project is authorized.

B.q: Why is starting up a project a lighter process than initiating a project?
options: Its decisions are delegated to team managers to save board time
Its outputs are informal and do not need board approval
It does the minimum needed to decide if initiation is worthwhile
Its business case is fixed and cannot be revised in initiation
B.why: Starting up a project does only the minimum necessary to decide whether it is worthwhile to initiate (13.1).

whyNot.0: Team managers are not involved in starting up; the business layer, executive and project manager are.
whyNot.1: The project brief and initiation stage plan are reviewed and approved by the board in authorize initiation.
whyNot.3: The outline business case is developed into the full business case during initiating a project.

B.q: Who provides the project mandate that triggers starting up a project?
options: The business layer
The project manager
The project board
The senior user
B.why: The mandate comes from the responsible authority in the business that commissions the project: the business layer (13.3).

whyNot.1: The project manager is appointed during starting up and works from the mandate; they do not issue it.
whyNot.2: The board is formed during starting up; the mandate exists before it.
whyNot.3: The senior user is a board role appointed during starting up, after the mandate is received.

C.q: Which product documents the business justification for initiating the project, and in which process is it prepared?
options: The full business case, in starting up a project
The outline business case, in initiating a project
The full business case, in directing a project
The outline business case, in starting up a project
C.why: Starting up a project prepares the outline business case, which justifies initiating; it becomes the full business case in initiating a project.

whyNot.0: The full business case is prepared later, in initiating a project.
whyNot.1: The outline business case is right, but it is prepared in starting up a project, not initiating.
whyNot.2: The board approves business cases in directing a project but does not prepare them, and the full one comes later.

C.q: Starting up a project ends when the project manager asks the board for authority to initiate. Which process receives that request, and which activity responds to it?
options: Directing a project, through authorize the project
Directing a project, through authorize initiation
Initiating a project, through agree the tailoring requirements
Controlling a stage, through authorize a work package
C.why: The request to initiate starts directing a project, and the board responds in authorize initiation by reviewing the brief and initiation stage plan.

whyNot.0: Authorize the project responds later, to the request for project authorization at the end of initiation.
whyNot.2: Initiating a project starts only after the board has authorized initiation.
whyNot.3: Controlling a stage belongs to delivery stages and is run by the project manager.

C.q: During starting up a project, the project manager finds that the assumed delivery date depends on a supplier contract that has already expired. Which objective of starting up a project does raising this now support?
options: Giving the business layer a connection to the project
Agreeing how baselines will be established and controlled
Avoiding time wasted initiating on unsound assumptions
Keeping attention on delivering the stage's products
C.why: Starting up a project should ensure time is not wasted initiating a project based on unsound assumptions about scope, timescales, acceptance criteria or constraints (13.2).

whyNot.0: A connection between the business layer and the project is an objective of directing a project.
whyNot.1: Agreeing how baselines are established and controlled is part of the common understanding reached in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: Keeping attention on the stage's products is an objective of controlling a stage.

reteach.title: A quick check before a bigger commitment
reteach.question: Why would an organization spend effort on a process that comes before the project even starts?

blocks.body: Initiation costs time and money. Starting up a project is the inexpensive filter in front of it: is there a reason to do this, who will lead it, how will we broadly go about it, and what will initiation involve? If the answers are weak, the board can decline to authorize initiation before much is spent.

blocks.text: Remember the two purposes as two questions: starting up asks 'viable and worthwhile?'; initiating builds 'solid foundations before significant spend'.

explain.body: Make sure the prerequisites for initiating are in place by asking whether the project is viable and worthwhile. The decision to start must be explicit, so the work happens before it. Starting up is as much about preventing poorly conceived projects as approving sound ones.

test.q: Besides approving viable projects, what is starting up a project designed to do?
options: Prevent poorly conceived projects being initiated
Prepare the detailed project plan for approval
Set the tolerances for each delivery stage
Appoint team managers for the first stage
test.why: Starting up a project is as much about preventing poorly conceived projects from being initiated as approving viable ones (13.1).

whyNot.1: The project plan is prepared in initiating a project.
whyNot.2: Stage tolerances are set by the board when it authorizes each stage plan.
whyNot.3: Team managers are engaged for delivery work through work packages, not in starting up.

explain.body: Justification for initiating (outline business case); authorities to initiate; enough information to define scope (project brief); approaches evaluated and the project approach agreed; people appointed for initiation and key roles; initiation work planned (stage plan); no time wasted on unsound assumptions.

test.q: Which is an objective of starting up a project?
options: The project initiation documentation is baselined
People are appointed to do the initiation work
The project product is accepted by the users
Highlight reports are sent at the agreed frequency
test.why: Starting up a project ensures individuals are appointed to undertake the initiation work or take significant project management roles (13.2).

whyNot.0: The PID is assembled and baselined in initiating a project.
whyNot.2: User acceptance of the project product is confirmed in closing a project.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports are produced in controlling a stage.

explain.body: Triggered by the project mandate from the business layer. It is pre-project and used by both the directing and managing levels. It ends with the request to initiate, and the board then reviews the project brief and initiation stage plan in authorize initiation.

test.q: Which products does the board review and approve when it decides whether to authorize initiation?
options: The PID and the first delivery stage plan
The project mandate and the lessons log
The full business case and project plan
The project brief and initiation stage plan
test.why: In authorize initiation the board reviews and approves the project brief and the initiation stage plan from starting up a project (14.4.1).

whyNot.0: The PID is reviewed when the board authorizes the project, at the end of initiation.
whyNot.1: The mandate is the input to starting up and the lessons log is a record; neither is what the board approves here.
whyNot.2: The full business case and project plan are prepared in initiating a project.

explain.body: Starting up is short, pre-project and asks whether the project is worth initiating. Initiating is the first stage and builds solid foundations (full business case, project plan, PID) before significant expenditure is committed.

test.q: How does starting up a project differ from initiating a project?
options: Starting up creates the PID; initiating creates the brief
Starting up checks it is worthwhile; initiating lays foundations
Starting up is the first stage; initiating is pre-project
Starting up is run by the board; initiating by team managers
test.why: Starting up a project checks the project is viable and worthwhile; initiating a project lays solid foundations before significant spend.

whyNot.0: It is the other way round: the brief comes from starting up and the PID from initiating.
whyNot.2: It is the other way round: starting up is pre-project and initiation is the first stage.
whyNot.3: Both are managing-level processes run by the project manager; starting up also involves the business layer and executive.
